_README: Curated registry of the LATEST labour-force period each National Statistical Office (NSO) has PUBLISHED. The pipeline compares this against ILOSTAT's latest period and lists everything in between as 'pending in ILOSTAT'. Only countries listed here get a pending badge; everything else shows 'not tracked'. Keys are ISO3 codes.

_schema.nso: Name/abbrev of the statistics office (shown in the UI)
_schema.nso_latest: Latest period the NSO has published: 'YYYY' | 'YYYYQn' | 'YYYYMmm'
_schema.periodicity: 'M' | 'Q' | 'A' — cadence used to enumerate the pending periods
_schema.source: URL to the NSO release / release calendar (shown as a link)
_schema.checked: YYYY-MM-DD this entry was last verified against the NSO site
_schema.note: free text (survey name, cadence quirks, caveats)

_policy: Every entry below was verified against an official NSO page. Countries whose correct value is uncertain are NOT listed here — they sit in _parked until resolved, because a wrong pending badge is worse than no badge.

IND.reason: PLFS moved from quarterly bulletins to a monthly bulletin series during 2025. The June 2026 monthly bulletin was confirmed on PIB, but the July 2026 press note could not be reached on an official domain — only secondary press. Need to confirm the monthly series is the right basis before tracking.

MEX.reason: INEGI runs two parallel tracks: monthly Indicadores de Ocupación y Empleo (latest June 2026) and the quarterly ENOE (latest 2026Q1). Which one ILOSTAT ingests determines the correct basis; picking the wrong one misstates the gap.

IDN.reason: Sakernas has February and August reference months (semi-annual). The registry schema only supports M/Q/A, and encoding it as monthly would enumerate every month in between and badly overstate the pending count. Needs schema support for a semi-annual cadence.

BHR.reason: The only current Bahraini source is the LMRA quarterly 'Labour Market Indicators', which is ADMINISTRATIVE work-permit data, not a household labour force survey. Wrong source family for the LFS index — it belongs to the Admin index if anywhere. The iGA household unemployment dataset on data.gov.bh is JS-rendered and robots-blocked, so no LFS period could be established.

KWT.reason: Latest LFS round appears to be 2016/2017, but the CSB page shows only publication listings (title, year, download count) rather than figures, and the LMIS portal could not be fetched. Confidence medium, not high.

ALB.reason: No Albanian observations present in Eurostat lfsi_emp_q (value object empty across the last 20 quarters). Needs a direct INSTAT check.

MNE.reason: No Montenegrin observations present in Eurostat lfsi_emp_q (value object empty across the last 20 quarters). Needs a direct MONSTAT check.

THA.reason: Q2 2026 summary posted 26/07/2026 but Thai-language only and not directly confirmed; medium confidence.

BGD.reason: bbs.gov.bd was rebuilt in 2026; the Labour & Employment page and publications listing render empty and the legacy portal is unreachable. Latest evidenced quarter is Oct-Dec 2024 via press. Newer 2025 quarters may exist.

PER.reason: Figure is LIMA METROPOLITANA ONLY, not national — wrong geographic scope for a country-level index. Also blocked on inei.gob.pe (HTTP 418), evidence secondary.

PRY.reason: ine.gov.py could not be opened by any route (browser navigation not permitted, curl proxy-blocked, WebFetch robots timeout). Q2 2026 rests on the state news agency and national press reporting an INE press conference on 31/07/2026.

DOM.reason: ENCFT is run by the CENTRAL BANK, not the NSO — decide whether that belongs in an NSO registry. Also evidence is secondary press; bancentral.gov.do returned navigation markup only.

ETH.reason: Highly irregular. Latest appears to be the 2022 Urban Employment Unemployment Survey; most recent full national LFS is 2021. Medium confidence.

CIV.reason: ANSTAT returned HTTP 403. Last published LFS appears to be ENE 2019; an ENE 2024 exists but ANSTAT confirmed results unpublished as of Oct 2025. Low confidence.

OMN.reason: Figures are ADMINISTRATIVE registered-employment records, not a household LFS — wrong source family for this index. Also ncsi.gov.om timed out.

YEM.reason: Yemen LFS 2013-14 published Oct 2015. cso-yemen.com returned 403 and the successor site could not be verified. Medium confidence.

SYR.reason: cbssyr.sy did not respond; cbssyr.org returned boilerplate with no publication list. No labour reference period could be evidenced at all.

AZE.reason: LFS tables published annually with an 'as of 1 January' reference date; latest is 1 Jan 2025 (reflecting 2024). Monthly figures on stat.gov.az are establishment-based, not LFS. Medium confidence.

KGZ.reason: LFS-based open-data tables end at 2024. Quarterly items on the employment pages are job-creation and registered-unemployment administrative statistics, not LFS. Medium confidence.

RUS.reason: Monthly Labour Force Survey — a genuine ILO-definition LFS. rosstat.gov.ru could not be fetched (robots/SSL); June 2026 rests on Interfax reporting the Rosstat release.

UZB.reason: Quarterly LFS exists alongside a separate registered-unemployment series. The stat.uz dataset listing shows update dates but no visible reference periods, so only Q4 2025 could be confirmed (via a Central Bank review). A Q1 2026 release is plausible but unverified.

AND.reason: Andorra does have a genuine LFS (Enquesta de forces del treball, annual). But estadistica.ad is a JS-rendered ArcGIS Hub site and the govern.ad article body did not render, so the 2025 reference year rests on the release title plus Andorran press.

MWI.reason: Malawi LFS 2024 — the first since 2013 — released 26/11/2025. nsomalawi.mw exposed no fetchable listing, so confirmation is via national press rather than the NSO page.

LSO.reason: 2024 LFS report dated July 2025, hosted on the Ministry of Finance site because bos.gov.ls is unreliable. Also catalogued by the ILO. Medium confidence — not confirmed on a Bureau of Statistics page.

SWZ.reason: Eswatini LFS 2025 results issued by government press release 22/06/2026, confirmed on ILO's page because gov.sz/CSO pages were not reliably fetchable.

SLV.reason: EHPM 2025 released by the BCR around April 2026, but ONEC's own EHPM landing page and downloads are stale (latest listed 2021) and bcr.gob.sv/documental could not be fetched. Also note DIGESTYC was absorbed into the CENTRAL BANK in Dec 2022 — same publisher-identity question as the Dominican Republic.

SUR.reason: Labour data come from the Huishoudonderzoek covering only Paramaribo & Wanica — not national coverage. ABS's own matrix says national employment statistics still rest on Census 2012. Very stale publisher.

CUB.reason: Encuesta Nacional de Ocupación 2024 and Anuario Estadístico 2024 both point to reference year 2024, but onei.gob.cu could not be fetched directly (robots failure); evidence is page titles plus official Cuban media.

NAM.reason: The 2023 labour force report is derived from the POPULATION AND HOUSING CENSUS, not a labour force survey — wrong source family for the LFS index (it belongs to the Census index). The last standalone Namibia LFS was 2018. Decide which basis to use.

NIC.reason: Two series with different answers: the monthly Encuesta de Empleo Mensual is current at June 2026, but the quarterly Encuesta Continua de Hogares was discontinued after 2022Q2. Which one counts changes the value by four years. Same class of problem as Mexico.

BLZ.reason: LFS is SEMI-ANNUAL (April and September rounds). The schema only supports M/Q/A; coding April 2026 as monthly would enumerate every month between and overstate the gap. Needs the same semi-annual schema support as Indonesia.

BHS.reason: LFS is SEMI-ANNUAL; the latest publication is a combined Q3+Q4 2025 report released 30/06/2026. Same schema problem as Belize and Indonesia. Note the legacy stats.gov.bs page is badly stale — the BNSI portal is authoritative.

MOZ.reason: No published labour force survey reference period could be established. ine.gov.mz is JS-heavy and its survey/publication listings were not retrievable; searches for 'Inquérito ao Emprego' returned Angola and Portugal results instead.

TKM.reason: No labour force survey and no employment/unemployment statistics published at all. The site carries only cabinet-meeting summaries.

LIE.reason: NO labour force survey exists. Liechtenstein's labour statistics are register-based (Beschäftigungsstatistik from AHV/employer registers, plus monthly registered unemployment). Deliberately not recorded rather than passing a register off as an LFS.

MCO.reason: NO labour force survey exists. The Observatoire de l'Emploi is entirely administrative, built from Caisses Sociales de Monaco and public-sector HR records.

SMR.reason: NO labour force survey exists. San Marino publishes labour statistics derived from Ufficio del Lavoro administrative registers.
